title: Deposits in round denominations that exceed the account's usual amounts
definition: Cash or cheque deposits whose amounts are exact multiples of a round figure, clustered in time and materially larger than the amounts usually seen on the account. The indicator measures the shape of the amounts; it does not establish their source.
evidence_to_cite: the deposit records forming the cluster
the account's historical amount distribution, over a stated period
the source of the funds as stated by the customer, where a statement exists
benign_explanations: A business that prices in round figures or invoices in round amounts.
A customer paying a rent, tuition or instalment in a round amount agreed in advance.
A cash-heavy retail account whose daily takings happen to settle at round figures.
A bank or building society teller machine that credits the change in a round amount.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, guidance on the avoidance of reporting requirements, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.

notes: Roundness on its own is close to meaningless; it is only useful in combination with frequency, dispersion across counterparties, and the account's baseline.
